2 · Paste the post copy

April 10th, the Air Force offered about 4,700 acres for AI data centers. August 4th, Alaska defended about 19,950 more.

What would run them? The lease solicitation says the JBER sites have "insufficient power" for a data center. AIDEA deputy director Brandon Brefczynski lists a power source among seven things the Mat-Su project doesn't have yet.

Who has the gas? Southcentral gas utility Enstar's president John Sims says "nobody has the gas right now that they're willing to sell."

The deck draws both parcels at one true scale, four gas prices as printed and storage against the stated target.

Comment on the DNR preliminary decision runs through August 19th.

What power condition belongs in that decision?

#CookInletGas #MatSuBorough #AIDataCenters

3 · Post, then paste this as the FIRST comment (within a minute)

Editor's note

GAS WATCH: PASS, read August 5th, 2026, 1 day on record, chart absent because one day is not yet a series. Read at desktop and phone width. The meter reads instantly and the big figure matches the tiles. One presentation fix shipped, the day-by-day table now says what a blank cell means, because with a single reading the residual column was empty and read as a reading that went missing rather than as a figure the model had no input for. gaswatch_build --self-test clean and the page check is 15 of 15 PASS. Nothing was touched on the collector, the model config or either gas ledger. THE FACT-CHECKER KILLED THE ORIGINAL FRAMING. The deck was selected around a marketed price of 4 to 5 cents per kilowatt-hour against 14 to 17 cents paid by large commercial users. Neither number exists in the cited source, which was fetched twice and contains none of the words cent, cents, kilowatt, kWh or megawatt. Thirteen claims were killed, including the bill number, the 90 percent tax exemption and an Edgmon quote that had only ever reached us through a summary of a rate-limited page. The replacement is stronger because every surviving claim comes from the selling side. THE CAPTION ROOM KILLED BOTH FIRST CANDIDATES. The critic found both closes were CAPTION_CRAFT's own menu examples with the nouns swapped, ruled that one crossed the no-verdict discipline, and named five standing ledger instructions the showrunner's brief had missed. The shipped caption is a reassigned third round on TIMELINE COLLAPSE, which has never shipped in 27 runs, with an invented close. DEGRADED AND SAYING SO. No copywriter, no pixel critics, no flow critic and no scorer subagent were spawned. The context budget went into the art build and into a GPU investigation. Every machine gate ran and passed. This is a real gap in the quality chain and it is disclosed here, in the artwork ledger and in the run record. ENGINE FINDING FOR PHASE 12. AKT.rig's shadow-casting key renders a black frame in this container. webglOK() returns true and the snapshot sentinel correctly catches it. Hand-rolled DirectionalLights render fine, which is how slide 06 reaches the GPU rung.

Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post Tuesday to Thursday, 8 to 11am Alaska time.
  • Paste the first comment immediately, within about 60 seconds of posting.
  • Reply substantively to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. A dead first hour is rarely recovered.
  • The single ask is the August 19th DNR comment window. If someone asks where to file, point them at the DNR preliminary decision, not at AIDEA.
  • If a commenter reads slide 03 as AIDEA admitting failure, correct it. Brefczynski's argument is that the project is early and that is exactly when public comment can shape it.
  • Do not let a thread drift into whether a data center will raise power bills. This deck is about whether the supply exists, not about who pays.
  • No adequacy verdict about the winter, in the post or in replies.
